author: petrikrohn_26497
message: ## 2 x 170HX (stock) > NVIDIA B300 SXM6 The above page shows test results for some GPUs and CPUs. At the top pf the list is Nvidia's latest and greatest flagship, the NVIDIA B300 SXM6. It shows a scalar (not tensor) FP16 fma compute of 75 TFLOPS. `| FP16   Compute   (half2 , fma  )                     75.201 TFLOPs/s ( 1x ) |`  This is the number that matters in LLM inference for token generation with a batch size of one, like in self-hosting LLMs. The same number for an *locked* (before unlocking) 170HX is about 50 TFLOPS, i.e. 2/3 of the B300.  The A100 and the 170HX outperform here, because their FP16 hfma performance is four times the FP32 fma performance. Most other Nvidia GPUs have 16-bit hfma somehow artificially capped to 1:1 of 32-bit fma.  For token generation, the other number that matters even more is memory bandwidth. Here the B300 beats the 170HX with 6543.01 GB/s vs. 1555 GB/s. But note, that 1555 GB/s is more than any consumer or pro card apart from the RTX 5090 / Pro 6000. Also the $40,000 H100/H200 PCIe card has higher bandwidth. All others are SXM.

author: beefbonecapone
message: yes this is most likely a binned card, 3x disabled GPC, a few TPCs disabled within some GPCs  ``` hierarchy terms for groups of GPU compute hardware:    GA100 GPU   └─ GPC — Graphics Processing Cluster      └─ TPC — Texture Processing Cluster         └─ SM — Streaming Multiprocessor    On a full GA100 design:    - 1 TPC contains 2 SMs.   - 1 GPC can contain 8 TPCs, or 16 SMs.   - The full physical design has up to 8 GPCs, 64 TPCs, and 128 SMs.    - A disabled GPC can hide as many as 16 SMs.   - A disabled TPC normally hides 2 SMs.   - Individual SM-level disable masks can potentially hide one SM at a time.   - Some SMs may remain visible but have specific operations—such as Tensor Core issue rate—throttled separately. ```

author: thanos8912
message: ``` Their 16-bit truncation is the root cause of their STRAP/LMR failure. The indirect engine truncates 32-bit addresses to 16 bits, so their writes to 0x9A0204, 0x100CE0, 0x823804, and 0x1FA824 go to wrong offsets (0x0204, 0x0CE0, 0x3804, 0xA824 — all BADF values). They need to use direct Falcon register writes (not the indirect engine) to reach the full 24-bit BAR0 address space.  The geometry registers and their correct values:  LMR: BAR0+0x100CE0, 0x28A = 40GB (currently 0x208 = 10GB) CFG1: BAR0+0x9A0204, 0x02669000 = 40GB (currently 0x02449000 = 10GB) CSTATUS: BAR0+0x9A020C, 0x800 = 40GB (currently 0x200 = 10GB) LMR must match CFG1 — when both are set to 40GB, the geometry survives GSP-RM boot. When they mismatch (LMR=10GB, CFG1=40GB), GSP-RM reads LMR and reverts CSTATUS.  FWSEC resets geometry — the VBIOS devinit ucode reads the VBIOS strap (0x44=10GB) and sets all three registers to 10GB during kgspPrepareForBootstrap. The geometry must be re-set AFTER FWSEC.  FBPA PLMs at 0x9A0148, 0x9A014C, 0x9A0008, 0x9A000C are 0xFF after FLR but become 0xFFFFFF8F after GSP-RM boot (bits 4,6 HS-locked).  Compute PLM (0x823804), SS0 (0x82381C), SS1 (0x823820) are all PL0-writable — we confirmed this directly. The compute unlock works from the host without HS code. ```
